facts.text: Croton’s post office was originally called Granby, then renamed in 1843 to avoid confusion with another Hartford in Trumbull County.
The Toledo & Ohio Central Railroad arrived in the late 19th century, moving Croton’s agricultural goods to Newark and Columbus before the station moved in the 1940s.
A Civil War Memorial in Croton honors township soldiers who fell or were taken prisoner, linking the village to national history.
On May 15, 1922, a Rum Plane crashed in Croton carrying 250 quarts of Canadian Scotch, drawing police, press, and curious locals.
